sections.text:
1 Hunc codicem Marcianum, anno 1416 antiquiorem, archetypum esse credide-
rim ex quo codicis Florentini, 7, ff. 99-219v descripta sunt, nam disiuncta et variis
temporibus exarata in libro Veneto apparent diversorum scriptorum excerpta quae
in Laurentiano sine intermissione subiunguntur. Textus capitulorum, quae quidem
contulimus, idem probare videtur. F. C.
sections.en: 1 I would believe that this Marcian codex, older than the year 1416, is the archetype from which the contents of the Florentine codex, 7, ff. 99-219v were copied, for disjointed and at various times written in the Venetian book appear excerpts of different writers which in the Laurentian are subjoined without interruption. The text of the chapters, which indeed we have compared, seems to prove the same. F. C.

summary.headline: Marcianus 324 Manuscript Entry
summary.text: Catalog entry for Marcianus 324, a late-fourteenth- or early-fifteenth-century paper manuscript, describing its folios, marginal notes, contents, added index, scribal hands, and bibliographic references. The listed works include astronomical handy tables, epochs of fixed stars, Theon of Alexandria, Isaac Argyros, astrolabe treatises, Ptolemy’s Tetrabiblos and Fruit, and Geminus’s Introduction to the Phenomena.
